messages:
Jordan: heads up, running the python quickstart sample-app and my first API call fails with a 403 even though the org shows billing enabled in the console. sample-app uses a service-account JSON key.

Anika: can you paste the error body? 403s can be due to billing_required or the token being scoped to a different workspace.

Jordan: body is `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"billing_required\",\"message\":\"workspace requires billing enabled\"}}` but the console shows my workspace 'acme-studio' with a valid card. Also tried my personal API key and got a 401.

Ravi: two things to check: (1) service account keys are bound to a workspace/org. If the key was created under a different workspace it will fail even if your current console org has billing. (2) sample-app reads REDWOOD_WORKSPACE env var — if that is unset it falls back to the default workspace on the key, which can be surprising after copying keys.

Jordan: ah, sample-app README just says set REDWOOD_API_KEY but not REDWOOD_WORKSPACE. I assumed the key was global.

Anika: quick repro steps: run `python sample-app/first_call.py` with `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=@path/to/service-account.json` vs `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-...` — different formats matter. For JSON keys we need REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_PATH to avoid mixing formats. Also the CLI `redwood whoami` will show the workspace tied to the token.

Jordan: ran `redwood whoami` and it printed `workspace: acme-studio` for my personal token and `workspace: acme-internal` for the service account. acme-internal doesn't have billing. That explains it. But the error message in the sample-app just surfaced HTTP 403 with no hint about workspace mismatch.

Ravi: agreed this is a DX hole. Proposal: sample-app should perform a preflight GET /v1/org (or /v1/workspace) and print `Workspace: <slug> — billing: enabled/disabled` before making the chat/generation call. If billing disabled, print console link and guidance to add payment method or request trial credits.

Anika: SDK-level improvement too: map `billing_required` -> BillingRequiredError containing `workspace_slug` when present, and include `https://console.redwood.ai/settings/billing?workspace=<slug>` as an actionable href. That way apps can surface the exact workspace.

Jordan: I'll open a quick PR to the sample-app to 1) require explicit env vars (`REDWOOD_API_KEY` vs `REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_PATH`, 2) show preflight workspace/billing check and 3) exit with clear error if mismatch.

devex-bot: Created ticket DX-2025 "Sample app should validate workspace and surface billing status for service accounts" and linked to repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/pull/2102 (draft).

billing-bot: Service account key `sa-acme-01` belongs to `acme-internal` — billing disabled. Billing status updated for `acme-studio` only.

Ravi: small note — there is a short propagation window after enabling billing (a minute or two). If users toggle billing immediately after creating a key they can see transient 403s. We should mention that in docs.

Jordan: fixed locally by pointing service-account to the right workspace and adding the preflight check. first call now returns 200. Will add a tiny troubleshooting section to the README about token formats, workspace env var, and billing propagation delay.

Anika: great. Action items: Jordan PR for sample-app README + preflight, SDK team to add BillingRequiredError mapping (Ben/SDK), and docs to mention propagation delay and service-account binding. Thanks for the clear repro steps. :thumbsup:
